_note: BIOLOGY ONLY. Compiled from general spearfishing-guide sources (not a validated regional survey), for Okinawa's subtropical Pacific/East China Sea reef fauna. Depth, temperature, substrate and season of presence and how each species responds to water clarity. None of it is law - Japanese prefectural rules on spearfishing are strict and vary, and are not encoded anywhere in this app. Humphead wrasse is deliberately not listed here even though it is a known local catch: it is IUCN-listed as Endangered and heavily protected in much of its Indo-Pacific range, and this app should not encourage targeting it.

species.note: Irabuchā - a shallow-reef grazer and traditional free-diving spearfishing target here, most active and most commonly hunted in the warmer months.
Mibai - several grouper species found in deeper reef crevices, holds tight to structure and holes.
Akajin - one of Okinawa's most prized reef fish, holding tight to coral and rock structure.
Taman - found over sand and rubble near reef edges rather than deep in structure.
Reef-associated snapper, common bottom-fish catch alongside grouper and emperor throughout the reef tract.
